item.title: Hundreds of fans welcome Brewers back to Milwaukee after World Series
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers relief pitcher Trevor Megill poked his head out of the ceiling of his bus and screamed at the hundreds of people in front of him. If Megill did that last time the Brewers landed at Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport, one day after the Brewers swept the Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, it would have been a waste of energy. Only two fans even tried to greet them. Not on Oct. 29. Two weeks later, less than 24 hours after the Brewers won the World Series over the Tampa Bay Rays , a swarm of fans lined up outside the airport's private terminal to coronate their champions' return. And Megill cheered right back. Buy Brewers World Series merchandise Two of the people Megill yelled to were Aaliyah Roosa, 9, and her 42-year-old mother Elena, who arrived at the airport just after 3 p.m. The two drove to Milwaukee from Racine after Aaliyah left elementary school. Hours earlier, Elena called her daughter's school to ask what Aaliyah would rather do once the bell rings. She could either stay after school for STEM club, or leave and watch the World Series champions' homecoming. Was that an easy choice? "Yeah," Aaliyah said. Elena knew it would be. She told Aaliyah about Milwaukee's Game 5 victory over Tampa Bay this morning; the game was too late for the third grader stay up and watch. Because Aaliyah couldn't wave her yellow towel at the end of the game, Elena, a lifelong fan with memories of Milwaukee County Stadium and many losses, did. Hours later, Elena was driving to Kohl's to get Aaliyah a World Series champion shirt before grabbing Elena to drive north. Minutes after watching the Brewers buses leave the airport, Elena teared up as she talked about what the moment meant to her. "There was always that hope, because they came so close all those years," Elena said. "It's awesome to finally, finally be able to celebrate the whole win. And not just almost." Bryan Garay got to Milwaukee's Mitchell International around the same time as the Roosas. The 36-year-old Waukesha native has lived in Milwaukee most of his life, and remembers more of the franchise's darker years than he'd like to. He was DJing at the Sofie in downtown when Jake Bauers caught the final out to clinch the championship, so Garay knew he'd go to the airport to welcome his favorite team home. He showed up in a Christian Yelich jersey on his body, a Milwaukee Brewers necklace around his neck and a blue flag in his hands, which he waved as the team's buses headed back to American Family Field. "Finally after 57 years of the franchise being in Milwaukee, we did it," Garay said. "We did ittttt!" Garay and the Roosas were part of a crowd of hundreds that took every parking spot in the airport observation area, and blocked the sidewalk along Layton Avenue. item.title: Bo Bichette back, as Mets 3B to exercise $42M option, per reports
item.description: Less than 24 hours after Brice Turang recorded the final out of the Brewers' first World Series title in franchise history on Wednesday night, Bo Bichette has already made his decision. Bichette will exercise his $42 million option to remain with the Mets, according to multiple reports. The Mets infielder had five days after the completion of the World Series to decide his fate for the offseason. The Athletic's Will Sammon was the first to report Bichette's intention to return. With no unrestricted free agents for the Mets heading into the upcoming campaign, Bichette's decision is the most impactful from the club's 2026 roster. Now, the two-time All-Star will run it back in Flushing. The two-time All-Star was the club's biggest splash before last season when he signed a three-year, $136 million deal which includes options for the final two seasons. Now, he'll return to the top of the lineup alongside Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto as the Mets hope for a healthier season to erase the failures of the last two campaigns. What was in Bo Bichette's decision to opt in It was a down season by Bichette's standard as he got acclimated in New York. While Bichette played 160 games, he stumbled out of the gate and finished with a .260/.312/.390 slash line including 18 home runs, 78 RBI and 76 runs. Through May, he had a .583 OPS, but he closed with a .772 OPS in the final four months. He also handled his first season at third base without issue. With that underperformance and uncertainty looming over how team payrolls and contracts could be structured in the future following this offseason's labor negotiations, it seemed unlikely that Bichette would fetch anywhere near the $42 million he would receive in 2027 elsewhere. Now, he has another chance to prove his past value, like he did in his walk year for the Blue Jays in 2025 when he was coming off an .840 OPS with 18 home runs and 94 RBI. He played a key role in their AL East crown on the way to the World Series. He has another $42 million After a rocky start that saw him booed early by Mets fans, Bichette seemed to find his footing down the stretch and appreciated the accountability of playing in the biggest market in baseball. He took a clear mentorship role in helping Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing get settled and appears unfazed by the pressure. What Bo Bichette might have left on the table In an underwhelming free agent class for position players, it could have been argued that Bichette would vaults to near the top of the market if he decided to opt out. For teams needing infield help, the top free agents include Teruaki Sato, Brandon Lowe, Jake Bauers, Luis Arraez and Jazz Chisholm Jr. It is possible that Bichette could have earned a longer contract elsewhere if he chose to opt out. Instead, he chose stability, comfort and one of the highest annual salaries for the 2027 season to stay in Flushing. item.title: Dylan Larkin 'no longer wants to be a Red Wing,' interim GM Shawn Horcoff says
item.description: DETROIT — The phone call came in the morning of Thursday, Oct. 29, and it was a shocker. Shawn Horcoff, the Red Wings' interim general manager, took the call from Pat Brisson, Dylan Larkin's agent, informing Horcoff that Larkin had upped the stakes in his formal request to be traded from the Red Wings, which has been there since June . "To put it simply, we received the call from Dylan's agent today just saying that Dylan no longer was going to be coming to the rink and no longer wants to be a part of the Red Wings," said Horcoff, in a brief press conference at Little Caesars Arena before the Wings faced the Chicago Blackhawks. The Wings suspended Larkin , 30, who will forfeit $41,237.11 for each day he sits out. Larkin has five years remaining on an eight-year contract worth an average of $8.7 million annually. The news from Larkin's side blindsided Horcoff. "For a large part Dylan kind of overcame the biggest hurdle, really, which was coming back and facing the initial (questions) from you guys and get on the ice for the first time with the fans," Horcoff said. "My initial plan was to try to fix it. I wanted to try to do what I could to keep Dylan here and in a Red Wing jersey, and clearly I was unsuccessful doing that." More: Dylan Larkin chooses to sit, drawing suspension from Red Wings The chance of reconciliation, or fixing this broken situation, seems farfetched. "I'll say at this point is Dylan no longer wants to be Red Wing, and he's not with us," Horcoff said. "I mean that pretty much you know is a strong statement. It's pretty cut and dry." Horcoff noticed Larkin becoming frustrated toward the end of the recent nine-day road trip the Wings had. "The last couple days and maybe on the road trip (you could) sense that things were a little bit off with him," Horcoff said. "He was growing maybe a little bit more frustrated. But I will say it was a bit of a surprise. "Probably the last couple days you kind of saw something a little bit different with Dylan, (and) Dylan's going to have to answer those questions on exactly what he was feeling." Trade talks are ongoing, Horcoff said, with the 10 teams on Larkin's preferred list to be dealt (Larkin has a no-trade clause). item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs’ decision to sign veteran NFL kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad has caught a lot of people by surprise, especially because of his history — off the field. Tucker was cut by the Baltimore Ravens in May of 2025 amid sexual misconduct accusations from over a dozen massage therapists. He was later suspended for 10 games by the NFL before being eligible for reinstatement last November. Tucker was able to get tryouts with the New Orleans Saints and the Indianapolis Colts since, but wasn’t signed. On Thursday, it was reported that the Chiefs were signing Tucker to a practice squad contract, a move that raised eyebrows. item.title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs Had an ‘Interesting’ Comment Ahead of His First Lambeau Field Game in 2026 Season
item.description: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs has finally seen action in the 2026 NFL season after getting removed from the NFL’s commissioner exempt list. Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season while he was placed on that list, stemming from his arrest in the offseason over misdemeanor charges after an altercation with his then-girlfriend in May. The three-time Pro Bowl tailback returned to action in Green Bay’s Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field in Detroit, and he’s about to make his first appearance at Lambeau Field in Green Bay for a Week 8 Thursday Night Football showdown against the visiting Carolina Panthers . “It’s going to be interesting. Obviously, like primetime, Lambeau Field, Thursday night, it’s gonna be electric,” the former Alabama Crimson Tide star running back told reporters via ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. “Looking forward to seeing our fans. Going out there and playing some good ball.” Josh Jacobs said he watched the games from home during his time on the commissioner exempt list, so Thursday will be his first time this season in Lambeau Field on game day. “It’s going to be interesting,” he said. On his home debut and the boos he heard in Detroit: pic.twitter.com/C9kHSdRgZt — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 27, 2026 Will Jacobs, Packers’ Rushing Attack Shine in Week 8? Green Bay Packers Josh Jacobs (8) participates in mandatory minicamp Thursday, June 11, 2026, at the Don Hutson Center in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Dan Powers/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin It will be interesting to see what kind of reception Jacobs will get from Packers fans. He was booed by Detroit fans in Week 7, and he could hear the same thing from at least a few fans in Green Bay. In any case, Jacobs is expected to help Green Bay’s run game that has been arguably the worst in the NFL thus far. The Packers are averaging fewer than 60 rushing yards per game and are also last in the NFL with only 2.9 yards per carry. Against the Lions, Jacobs and company came up with only 60 rushing yards on 19 carries. Jacobs had 36 rushing yards on 11 carries in that contest. However, there is a reason to believe that Green Bay will have a great night on the ground versus the Panthers, as Carolina is allowing over 150 rushing yards per game. item.title: Jaissle on Newcastle injury worry and Carabao Cup exit
item.description: Jaissle on Newcastle injury worry and Carabao Cup exit Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has confirmed Will Osula suffered an ankle injury during their 3-1 Carabao Cup defeat to Everton. Osula was unable to continue after twisting his ankle while taking a shot, with Jaissle admitting it is too early to know the severity of the problem. “It’s too early at the moment,” Jaissle said. “He was not able to continue. He twisted his ankle when he took the shot.” Jaissle was also left frustrated by Newcastle’s overall performance, believing the defeat reflected a recurring problem this season. “We are, of course, disappointed with the result,” he said. “It’s also a bit shocking at the moment, because overall the game was not that bad. “But it’s a bit the story of the season so far, in situations where it really counts, we lack in the clinical approach to solve the situations.” The Newcastle boss was particularly unhappy with the manner in which his side conceded. “Just think about the first one, this is again a low-risk zone where we said, clear the ball, nothing happens, and a couple of seconds later you can see the goal out of nothing,” Jaissle said. “The second one is also frustrating, because in my point of view we deserve to have a penalty on the other hand, and then you miss that in the transition to defend our own box, which is again for me difficult to accept. “We have clear rules on how to behave in these matters. “And the third one, again a critical ball loss when you’re in possession, and the opposition is punishing you at that level pretty quickly.” Jaissle also felt Newcastle failed to make the most of the chances they created. “These are the things we need to learn quickly,” he said. “On the other hand I think you all saw also the game and the statistics. We had many, many opportunities to score, big chances as well. “And also in their box we need to be more clinical to get a different result.”

item.description: (Photo by Allen Berezovsky/Getty Images) Ric Flair shared an update after a frightening fall outside a Tampa restaurant left him hospitalized with injuries to his head and eye . The 77-year-old wrestling legend took to social media Saturday (Oct. 24) to reassure fans that he's recovering at home following Friday's incident. Flair shared a photo of himself sitting in a chair with a circular bandage covering his right eye. "Thank you all for the messages and prayers! I will get back to you all individually as I get stronger," Flair wrote. "Thank you to Tampa General Hospital staff and doctors that put up with me until 4:30 a.m. I appreciate you all and thank you for everything you did. The WWE Hall of Famer reportedly fell shortly afterward, suffering cuts to his head and the area surrounding his eye. Emergency responders arrived at the scene and transported Flair to a nearby hospital by ambulance. His daughter, WWE star Charlotte Flair, provided an update shortly after the fall, letting fans know her father was stable while sharing a joke he made to his doctor. "Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head… (ps: he's going to be ok)," she wrote on X, referencing her father's history with the late Ultimate Warrior. The incident occurred just hours after Flair revealed that he was dealing with a blood clot in his leg, forcing him to cancel a scheduled appearance at Washington State Horror Con in Seattle. item.title: Skip Bayless Gets Critical of Cowboys Despite Win vs. Eagles
item.description: Skip Bayless criticized the Dallas Cowboys following their 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, pointing to the circumstances surrounding the matchup and Philadelphia’s quarterback situation. Dallas snapped a two-game losing streak with the victory, while the Eagles played without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts. Bayless also addressed Philadelphia backup quarterback Tanner McKee, who started in place of Hurts. McKee finished 23-of-35 passing for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception as the Eagles fell to Dallas. His performance included a third-quarter stretch that helped Philadelphia take a 21-20 lead before the Cowboys regained control. item.title: Brewers-Rays Game 5 clincher ends World Series on viewership high note
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn The Milwaukee Brewers’ World Series clincher on Wednesday made this year’s Fall Classic relatively on par with other World Series this decade in viewership, with the usual boost from Nielsen’s recent methodology updates. The Brewers’ title-clinching Game 5 win over the Tampa Bay Rays averaged 14.22 million viewers across Fox and Fox Deportes, according to preliminary figures the network released. If the figure holds, Game 5 would be functionally even with last year’s Dodgers-Blue Jays Game 5, which averaged 14.30 million viewers, and would surpass all Game 5 audiences between 2019 and 2023. “Unshakeable! Unstoppable! Champions at last!” Preliminary numbers indicate 14.2 million viewers watched @FOXSports’ coverage of #WorldSeries Game 5 as the @Brewers captured their first championship in franchise history. https://t.co/lAulfGLvT1 — FOX Sports PR (@FOXSportsPR) October 29, 2026 When including the preliminary figure from Game 5, the full five-game series averaged 11.83 million viewers across Fox, Fox Deportes, and Univision, which would put the series’ viewership level with Astros-Phillies in 2022 (11.76 million viewers) and Braves-Astros in 2021 (11.74 million viewers), both of which had six games. Viewership will predictably fall short of Dodgers-Yankees in 2024 (15.10 million viewers) and Dodgers-Blue Jays last year (15.49 million viewers), but will easily surpass Rangers-Diamondbacks in 2023 (9.08 million viewers), the least-watched World Series of all time. Of course, given Nielsen’s recent methodological changes, this year’s World Series was likely less watched than both 2021 and 2022, despite being level with those years on paper. Since then, Nielsen has expanded its out-of-home viewing measurements to cover 100% of the country and also began incorporating its Big Data sample into the top-line viewership figure. Both changes have generally increased viewership for live sports compared to prior years, particularly for major live events like the World Series. However, both the 2021 and 2022 World Series went six games and benefited from higher viewership in Game 6, lifting the overall average. It’s safe to say the Brewers-Rays outperformed expectations, especially since the series went only five games. Before the series, many feared two smaller-market teams with no clear superstars might replicate 2023 viewership levels. That proved not to be the case, with all but one game eclipsing 10 million viewers.
